biggest_catch: The match is dollar-for-dollar on YOUR contributions — you must put in up to $500 of your own money to get the $500. The award is also subject to availability of funds, is paid into a CollegeInvest-owned account that can only be disbursed directly to a college, and the beneficiary must be 8 or younger at first application.
catches: Dollar-for-dollar match on your own contributions: contribute $350, get $350; contribute $0, get $0. It is a savings boost on planned college savings, not free money.
Subject to availability of funds — eligibility confirmation does not guarantee the award.
Must apply during the annual application period (typically October through December) and REAPPLY every year with fresh federal tax forms; no application, no award.
Income-eligible only: family AGI at or below the program-year income chart; chart updates yearly.
Beneficiary must be 8 years old or younger at the time of the initial application (up to 18 in later years); account must already be open at application time.
Only account-owner contributions qualify — Upromise, Ugift, employer promotions, and other third-party contributions do not.
Award goes into a separate CollegeInvest-owned account and can only be disbursed directly to institutions of higher education (tuition/fees) — not to you.
Use-it-or-lose-it: funds must start being used within 4 years of age of maturity (typically 18) and be fully used within 6 years, or they are revoked.
Standard 529 tax risk: earnings withdrawn for non-qualified expenses face federal income tax plus a 10% federal penalty (and possible state tax consequences) — consult a tax professional.

steps: Open a CollegeInvest 529 Savings account with yourself as owner and your child (8 or younger at first application) as beneficiary.

During the annual application period (typically October–December), submit the Matching Grant application with your CollegeInvest account number and PDFs of federal tax forms for all parents/guardians in the household.
Contribute to the account during the program year (typically the calendar year) — up to $500 of account-owner contributions to earn the full $500 match.

The matching award is deposited into a CollegeInvest-owned account for your child in the first quarter after the program year ends; it can only be disbursed directly to an institution of higher education.
